events.summary: A severe winter storm/cold snap affected Texas during February 12–17.
events.quote: Texas had one of, if not the, coldest and most impactful winter storms observed in state history during the week of February 12–17.

events.summary: Record winter demand and generation unit outages cascaded into grid instability and power losses across ERCOT.
events.quote: A combination of record winter demand and generation unit outages cascaded into instability and power losses across the ERCOT power grid

events.summary: At the peak, 4.5 million Texans were without electricity.
events.quote: resulting in 4.5 million Texans without electricity at the peak.

events.summary: Natural gas production fell significantly during the event, and power outages made the decline worse.
events.quote: Although natural gas production fell significantly during this event, the timeline indicates that power outages made this decline worse.

events.summary: All power generation resources showed lower output during the worst of the cold snap while demand peaked.

time.time_text: During the worst of the cold snap

events.quote: During the worst of the cold snap, all power generation resources showed a decline in output while demand peaked to unprecedented levels.

events.summary: ERCOT meteorologists reportedly warned market participants and the public of the year's coldest weather.
events.quote: ERCOT meteorologists reportedly warns Market Participants and the public of the coldest weather of the year.

events.summary: ERCOT issued an Operating Conditions Notice for an approaching extreme cold weather system.
events.quote: February 8: ERCOT issues an Operating Conditions Notice (OCN) for an extreme cold weather system approaching Thursday, February 11 through Monday, February 15 with temperatures anticipated to remain 32° F or below.

events.summary: ERCOT issued an Advisory for predicted extreme weather in the ERCOT Region.
events.quote: February 10: ERCOT issues an Advisory for the predicted extreme weather for the ERCOT Region.

events.summary: Governor Greg Abbott declared a state of emergency in all Texas counties ahead of severe winter weather.
events.quote: February 12: Governor Greg Abbott declares a state of emergency in all Texas counties ahead of the expected severe winter weather.

events.summary: Natural gas supply began declining from February 12 through February 15, with February 14 the most impactful day.
events.quote: February 12: Natural gas supply begins declining through February 15, with February 14 being the most impactful day.

events.summary: Natural gas supply declined by about 0.2 Bcf/d and 0.7 Bcf/d on February 12 and 13.
events.quote: Natural gas supply declined ~0.2 Bcf/d and ~0.7 Bcf/d on February 12 and 13, respectively, leading up to February 14.

events.summary: Power generation failures occurred across the board.
events.quote: The declines on February 13, although material, were not large enough to cause the power generation failures seen across the board.

events.summary: On February 14, as early as 1:00 AM, power generation reported output limitations or significant capacity was forced offline by extreme weather.
events.quote: February 14: As early as 1:00 AM, power generation reported output limitations or significant capacity was forced offline by the extreme weather.

events.summary: At its highest point, more than 48.6% of all generation in ERCOT was in forced outage.
events.quote: At its highest point more than 48.6% of all generation in ERCOT was in forced outage.

events.summary: Natural gas declines showed about 2 Bcf/d declines.
events.quote: Natural gas declines showed ~2 Bcf/d declines.

events.summary: ERCOT entered Emergency Operations Level 3 at 01:20 AM.

time.time_text: February 15: ERCOT enters Emergency Operations Level 3 at 01:20 AM

events.quote: February 15: ERCOT enters Emergency Operations Level 3 at 01:20 AM

events.summary: ERCOT returned to normal operations at 10:35 AM on Friday, February 19.
events.quote: does not return to normal operations until 10:35 AM Friday, February 19.

events.summary: At least 4.5 million customers were without power and more than 13 million had water service interruptions.
events.quote: At least 4.5 million customers were without power and more than 13 million customers had water service interruptions.

events.summary: On Saturday, February 13 at 08:43, ERCOT Physical Responsive Capability fell below 3 GW for the first time that weekend.
events.quote: Sat. 13 Feb. 2021 08:43 ERCOT Physical Responsive Capability (PRC), which is a measure of online capacity that is available to respond quickly to disturbances, falls below 3 GW for the first time during the weekend.

events.summary: ERCOT was at EEA Level 1 with reserves below 2,300 MW at 00:15.
events.quote: Energy Emergency: EEA Level 1: At 00:15, ERCOT at EEA 1 - Reserves below 2, 300 MW.

events.summary: ERCOT was at EEA Level 2 with reserves below 1,750 MW at 01:07 and load resources were deployed.
events.quote: EEA Level 2: At 01:07, ERCOT at EEA 2 Reserves below 1, 750 MW. Load resources are being deployed.
